paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's love doesn't have an expiration date. He says, "I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have drawn you with loving devotion" (Jeremiah 31:3). Everything else in this passage grows out of that one line, the rebuilding, the dancing, the road home. And the people He's talking to are people who got scattered, so His love is not something they earned by behaving.

Now look at who gets to come home. The blind, the lame, expectant mothers, women in labor, and God says, "They will return as a great assembly!" (Jeremiah 31:8). He even makes the path level so nobody stumbles (Jeremiah 31:9). Then Ephraim shows up moaning about his own mistakes, and God answers, "Is not Ephraim a precious son to Me, a delightful child?" (Jeremiah 31:20). He doesn't make Ephraim earn his way back first. The weak, the weeping and the ashamed are exactly the ones He's gathering up.

So if you're carrying some grief today, hear what He told Rachel: "So there is hope for your future, declares the LORD" (Jeremiah 31:17). He sees the weeping and doesn't wave it away. He promises, "I will turn their mourning into joy" (Jeremiah 31:13), and He says, "I will refresh the weary soul and replenish all who are weak" (Jeremiah 31:25). Friend, the weary soul is welcome in His kitchen, so lean on Him and keep your ovens ready.
